findings.title: Hierarchical Taxonomy of Psychopathology (HiTOP) — State of the Science and Clinical Applications
findings.venue: Annual Review of Clinical Psychology / Behavior Therapy / Frontiers in Psychiatry
findings.key_findings: HiTOP has advanced significantly with: (1) B-HiTOP (Brief HiTOP) validated 2025 — 45-item self-report measuring 6 primary spectra (Internalizing, Somatoform, Detachment, Thought Disorder, Disinhibition, Antagonism) with Cronbach's alpha .82-.90; (2) HiTOP-SR (Self-Report) measure developed for clinical use; (3) Scoping review (Argyriou et al. 2025, Frontiers) demonstrates HiTOP dimensions across specificity levels (superspectrum to component) as moderators of differential CBT response for internalizing disorders; (4) HiTOP constructs show stronger associations with genetic/neurobiological markers than DSM diagnoses; (5) HiTOP Society formed to organize consortium efforts; (6) Clinical utility demonstrated — clinicians rate HiTOP as more useful for describing psychopathology and assessing global functioning than DSM categories.

findings.title: HiTOP and Personalized Mental Health Treatment Selection
findings.key_findings: Scoping review (Argyriou et al. 2025, DOI: 10.3389/fpsyt.2025.1597879) examined HiTOP-relevant moderators of differential psychotherapy response for internalizing disorders. Found preliminary evidence that HiTOP dimensions at multiple specificity levels (superspectrum, spectrum, subfactor, syndrome, component) can inform personalized treatment selection. Identified key gaps: limited research in several HiTOP domains (especially Disinhibition, Antagonism, Thought Disorder), strict inclusion/exclusion criteria reducing heterogeneity, large variability in HiTOP dimension measurement, and methodological limitations for assessing personalized treatment response. Seven recommendations proposed for advancing precision mental health with HiTOP.

findings.title: RDoC Framework Updates — Sensorimotor Domain and Reorganization
findings.key_findings: NIMH officially added Sensorimotor domain to RDoC framework to foster earlier identification of motor systems disruptions in psychopathology. The domain includes constructs: Sensorimotor Dynamics, Habit-Sensorimotor, Innate Motor Patterns, Agency and Ownership — mapped to neural circuits (cerebellum, basal ganglia, motor cortex, parietal cortex) and measured via tasks like sensory-motor adaptation, 2-step task, video-based tic rating. RDoC framework continues as dynamic, continually developing system with reorganization of Positive Valence domain content. RDoC Matrix redesigned in user-friendly format. RDoC-guided research increasingly applied in early-phase neuropsychiatric drug development (Magaraggia 2026).

findings.title: DSM-5 Critiques and Dimensional Alternatives
findings.venue: Psychiatric Times / Psychiatry at the Margins / Journal of Nervous and Mental Disease
findings.key_findings: DSM-5-TR (2022) introduced only limited dimensionality (substance use, autism spectrum, neurocognitive disorders, personality disorders Alternative Model). Core critiques persist: (1) semi-arbitrary diagnostic thresholds; (2) heavy comorbidity from overlapping categories; (3) within-disorder heterogeneity; (4) poor validity — genetic findings don't map onto DSM categories; (5) diagnostic instability over time. HiTOP and RDoC presented as leading alternatives. Key distinction: DSM's "dimensional" approach often means simple severity ratings on categorical diagnoses, whereas HiTOP/RDoC propose psychometrically validated dimensional constructs embedded in structural models. DSM-5-TR public comment period open through April 2026 for autism severity specifier clarifications.

findings.title: Comparing Categorical, Dimensional, and Hybrid Models for Internalizing Pathology
findings.key_findings: De la Rosa-Cáceres et al. (2025) compared latent class analysis (categorical), confirmatory factor analysis (dimensional), and hybrid models against current HiTOP model. Found dimensional and hybrid models better capture internalizing pathology structure than purely categorical approaches. Supports HiTOP's hierarchical dimensional framework over DSM's categorical system. Highlights that hybrid models incorporating both categorical and dimensional elements may offer pragmatic bridge for clinical transition.

findings.title: Meta-Mesh Ontology (MMO) — Integrative Framework for Psychiatric Knowledge
findings.key_findings: MMO introduced as modular, BFO-compliant meta-ontology unifying heterogeneous psychiatric knowledge bases. Acts as middleware between Basic Formal Ontology (BFO) and domain-specific ontologies. Core Domain Framework (CDF) serves as top-level architecture. Maps to/integrates: DSM, ICD, HiTOP, RDoC, SNOMED CT, LOINC, UMLS, Gene Ontology, Social Determinants of Health Ontology (SOHO), Adverse Childhood Experiences Ontology (ACESO), ISO 37120. Enables cross-domain reasoning across biological, psychological, social domains. Supports multimodal data integration from clinical, environmental, sensor sources. Authoritative OWL/RDF artifacts available on GitHub. Developed at Jena University Hospital / German Center for Mental Health (DZPG).

findings.title: Mental Functioning Ontology (MF) — 2026 Update
findings.key_findings: MF ontology for mental functioning (cognition, intelligence, mental processes, traits, mental disorders) developed under OBO Foundry principles, BFO-compliant, aligned with Ontology for General Medical Science (OGMS). Modules: MFO-MD (mental disorders, reusing Disease Ontology IDs), MFO-EM (emotion ontology). Actively aligned with Cognitive Atlas, Cognitive Paradigm Ontology, Neural Electro Magnetic Ontologies. Maintainer: Janna Hastings (UCL). Version IRI updated February 2026. Available in OWL format via OntoBee, AberOWL, OLS, BioPortal, Bioregistry.

findings.title: GALENOS Mental Health Ontology — Upper-Level Structure and Protocol
findings.key_findings: GALENOS (Global Alliance for Living Evidence on aNxiety, depressiOn and pSychosis) developing ontology to structure living systematic reviews. Protocol (Schenk et al. 2025) defines 8-step development process. Upper-level ontology (Santilli et al. 2026) includes 25 key classes across: research studies, human populations (with personal histories), mental health interventions (content, delivery, mechanisms, outcomes, engagement), and intervention scenarios. Nine relationship types connect entities. Reuses Mental Functioning Ontology, Emotion Ontology, Behaviour Change Intervention Ontology (BCIO), Information Artifact Ontology (IAO). Machine-readable, integrated into data repository for automated evidence synthesis. GitHub repository active: github.com/galenos-project/mental-health-ontology.

findings.title: Cognitive Ontology Pluralism — Theoretical and Empirical Case
findings.venue: Neuroscience and Philosophy (MIT Press) / Philosophy of Science / Center for Philosophy of Science seminars
findings.key_findings: McCaffrey & Wright (2022) and subsequent work argue taxonomic pluralism is necessary — no single cognitive ontology can carve mind at brain's joints. Different cognitive neuroscience subfields have different predictive/explanatory goals, requiring different ontologies. Key arguments: (1) neural reuse hypothesis — brain regions recombine across tasks; (2) epistemic communities form around shared goals, each implementing distinct knowledge-building strategies; (3) coordinated pluralism (Sullivan 2017) proposed over uncoordinated pluralism; (4) data-driven discovery methods (e.g., meta-analytic clustering, computational modeling) offered as path forward. Seminar series at Pitt Center for Philosophy of Science (2025-2026) features talks on neural degeneracy, atlas-of-mind approaches, and pluralistic taxonomies.

findings.title: Ontology of Mental Health and Well-Being — GALENOS and WHO Frameworks
findings.key_findings: GALENOS ontology explicitly includes wellbeing constructs beyond dysfunction (human mental health conceptualizations: symptoms, diagnoses, wellbeing). WHO definition (2022) adopted: "state of mental well-being enabling people to cope with stresses, realize abilities, learn/work well, contribute to community." GALENOS upper-level ontology structures populations, interventions, settings, and outcomes — including positive outcomes and spillover effects. Systematic reviews cover topics: circadian disruption in mood disorders, cardiovascular-metabolic factors in psychosis, cognitive bias modification for social anxiety, internet use and youth mental health, heat and mental health. Integrates BCIO for intervention content/delivery specification.

findings.title: Beyond DSM and ICD: Comprehensive Review of Alternative Classification Systems
findings.key_findings: Review (2025, DOI: 10.1007/s12144-025-07787-y) surveys HiTOP, RDoC, and other alternatives. Highlights HiTOP's compatibility with RDoC — HiTOP provides dimensional phenotypic structure, RDoC provides neurobiological mechanisms; together they bridge levels of analysis. Notes HiTOP's clinical applicability: prioritizes functional impairment over diagnosis, includes subthreshold profiles, compatible with transdiagnostic treatments (e.g., Unified Protocol). RDoC's sensorimotor domain addresses motor dysfunction in psychosis, depression, neurodevelopmental disorders. Both frameworks positioned as complementary rather than competing replacements for DSM/ICD.

summary: As of September 2026, psychological ontology has converged on three parallel tracks: (1) HiTOP has matured into a clinically deployable dimensional system with validated measures (B-HiTOP, HiTOP-SR) and demonstrated utility for personalized treatment selection, though gaps remain in non-internalizing domains; (2) RDoC continues evolving as a living framework with the Sensorimotor domain now formally integrated and increasing application in drug development; (3) Formal ontology engineering has produced multiple interoperable artifacts — Meta-Mesh Ontology (BFO-compliant middleware integrating DSM, ICD, HiTOP, RDoC, and biomedical ontologies), Mental Functioning Ontology (OBO Foundry-aligned, updated 2026), and GALENOS Mental Health Ontology (upper-level published 2026, supporting living systematic reviews). Cognitive ontology pluralism is now the dominant philosophical position, rejecting a single unified taxonomy in favor of coordinated, purpose-relative ontologies. The field is moving from critique of DSM/ICD toward practical integration: HiTOP for phenotypic structure, RDoC for mechanistic mapping, and formal ontologies (MMO, MF, GALENOS) for computational interoperability and evidence synthesis.
